title: 第5章 生意热闹第6章 韩老五入门
content_zh:
次日清晨。
羊圈街尚泛着冷灰，街两旁的店铺门板还紧闭着。
路沉已在街心摆开了阵仗。
拴虎扯来的丈长红布哗迎风抖开，挂在堵土墙上。红布上，用墨汁写着八十个字，每个字都有碗口大。
秃子不知从哪借来一面破锣，哐哐敲得震天响，扯着沙哑的嗓子油腔滑调地吆喝起来
“一文钱搏三十文，开彩见真章。”
清冷的街道渐渐聚了人。
赶早路的、做小买卖的，都围上来看热闹，对着那幅红布指指戳戳。
“一文钱搏三十文？骗鬼呢！”
“八成是江湖骗子的新把戏。”
“就是，准是哪个瘪犊子想钱想疯了！”
七嘴八舌，哄笑不绝。
可当大伙儿看清红布后面坐着的是路沉时。
就像被掐住脖子的鸭子，瞬间安静了不少。
只因在这羊圈街，路沉虽为混混，但做事讲规矩。
就冲着他这块招牌，这事情，好像有几分真了。
去年秋凉时分，一伙外地泼皮在老孙头的馄饨摊上吃了馄饨，不想给钱。
老孙头上前理论，他们反而诬陷馄饨不干净，动手就把摊子砸了。汤锅、桌凳顿时碎了一街。
是路沉带着人追出三条街，不仅将那伙无赖揍得跪地求饶，让他们不光赔够了摊子的损失，连带老孙头受的惊吓也一并算了钱。
这恩情，老孙头记到今天。

这会儿，见大伙还在嘀咕。
老孙头颤着手在怀里摸索了一阵，捻出一枚磨得亮晶晶的铜子。
当啷一声扔进箱子。
他扯着嗓子道“都瞅啥？路爷的场子，能有假？”
说罢，老孙头用粗黑的手指，小心翼翼地在铺开的红布上，点了一个歪歪扭扭的“孙”字。
那是他这辈子唯一认得、也会写的字。
还有几个曾受过路沉照拂的小贩，抱着试一试的态度，也拿出了一文钱。
叮叮当当，好几枚铜钱落进木箱。
巳时一到。
在路沉的示意下，瞎子蒙上黑布，枯瘦的手在纸条堆里摸索。
从中抽出一张红纸条，缓缓展开，上面正好是个“孙”字。
“我，啊？中奖了。”
老孙头身子一颤，像是被什么砸中了脑袋，张着嘴愣在原地，半晌才挤出半句话
“这……真让我撞上了？”
路沉走上前，亲手将三十枚铜钱，一枚一枚地数给他。
钱不多，老孙头一双手就捧得过来。
他捧着那三十枚铜钱，咧开的嘴就没合拢过。
content_en:
Early next morning.
Yangquan Street is still glowing with cold gray, and the shop doors on both sides of the street are still tightly closed.
Lu Chen has already set up a battle array in the middle of the street.
The ten-foot-long red cloth pulled by the tiger fluttered in the wind and hung on the earthen wall. Eighty characters were written in ink on the red cloth, each character was as big as the mouth of a bowl.
The bald man borrowed a broken gong from somewhere, banged it loudly, and started shouting in a greasy voice with a hoarse voice.
"One penny is worth thirty cents, and the lottery will reveal the true result."
People gradually gathered in the deserted streets.
Those who were on their way in the morning and those doing small business gathered around to watch the excitement and pointed at the red cloth.
"Thirty cents for one cent? What a liar!"
"Eighty percent of it is a new trick of charlatans."
"That's right, some bastard must be crazy about money!"
There was a lot of chatter and laughter.
But when everyone saw clearly that Lu Chen was sitting behind the red cloth.
Like a duck being strangled by the neck, it suddenly became quieter.
Just because in this Yangquan Street, although Lu Chen is a gangster, he behaves according to the rules.
Just for his signature, this thing seems to be somewhat true.
In the cool autumn last year, a group of out-of-town gangsters ate wontons at Lao Suntou's wonton stall, not wanting to pay.
Lao Sun came forward to argue, but they falsely accused the wontons of being unclean and smashed the stall. The soup pots, tables and stools were shattered all over the street.
It was Lu Chen who led the men and chased them through three streets. Not only did they beat the gangsters until they knelt down and begged for mercy, they were not only compensated for the loss of the stall, but also the shock to Old Sun's head.
Lao Suntou remembers this kindness to this day.
At this moment, I saw that everyone was still muttering.
With his head trembling, Old Sun groped for a while in his arms and pulled out a polished copper.
It was thrown into the box with a clang.
He raised his voice and said, "What are you looking at? How can Mr. Lu's situation be fake?"
After that, Old Sun used his thick black fingers to carefully tap a crooked word "Sun" on the spread red cloth.
That was the only word he knew and could write in his life.
There were also several hawkers who had been cared for by Lu Shen, and they also took out a penny with the attitude of giving it a try.
Ding-dang-dang, several copper coins fell into the wooden box.
The time has come.
At Lu Chen's signal, the blind man covered himself with a black cloth and groped among the pile of notes with his skinny hands.
He pulled out a piece of red paper and slowly unfolded it. It happened to have the word "grandson" written on it.
"I, ah? I won the prize."
Old Sun's head and body trembled, as if something hit him on the head. He froze on the spot with his mouth open. It took him a long time to squeeze out a few words.
"This...really hit me?"
Lu Chen stepped forward and counted the thirty copper coins to him one by one with his own hands.
The money was not much, but Lao Suntou could hold it in both hands.
He held the thirty copper coins in his hands, his grin never closing.
